full_judgment:
That on 31-8-78 plaintiff instituted title suit No. 152 of 1978 in the court of 3rd Sub-ordinate Judge, Dacca against defendant Nos. 1 and 2 for a decree for specific performance of a contract in respect of certain household property on the basis of an agreement dated 10-2-73 entered into between plaintiff and defendant No. 1. On application under Order 1, rule 10 CPC filed by the plaintiff on 28-11-78 defendants Nos. 3, 4 and 5 were added as parties in the suit on 29-11-78. 

 "1. Save as otherwise provided by any enactment for the time being in force, an appeal from a decree of order of a District Judge or Additional Judge shall lie to the High Court. 

 2. An appeal shall not lie to the High Court from a decree or order of an Additional Judge in any case in which if the decree or order had been made by the District Judge an appeal would not lie to that court." 

 "1. Save an aforesaid, an appeal from a decree or order of a Sub-ordinate Judge shall lie- 

 a) To the District Judge where the value of the original suit in which or in any proceeding arising out of which the decree or orders was made did not exceed Taka twenty thousand and 

 2. Save as aforesaid, an appeal from a decree or order of a Munsif shall lie to the District Judge. 

 4. The High Court may with the previous sanction of the Government direct by notification in the official gazette, that appeals lying to the District Judge under sub-section (2) from all or any of the decrees or orders of any Munsif shall be preferred to the court of such sub-ordinate Judge as may be mentioned in the notification and the appeals shall there-upon be preferred accordingly. 

 8. All orders are not appealable. Appeal lies only against those orders which are enumerated in Order XLIII, rule 1 CPC. Section 96 CPC provides for appeal against original decree Revision lies against non-appealable orders. Previously revision against non-appealable orders lay only in the High Court Division. In case of an appealable order passed by a Sub-ordinate Judge, an appeal shall lie to the District Judge where the value of the original suit in which or in any proceeding arising out of which the order was made did not exceed Taka 20,000 and to the High Court in any other case. Can it be conceived that a court which cannot exercise jurisdiction over a matter in appeal was intended to exercise its revisional jurisdiction. It appears to be inconsistent with the scheme of the Code of Civil Procedure and Civil Courts Act to invest the District Judge with concurrent revisional jurisdiction in matters where no appeal lies before the District Judge. Hitherto to the District Judge has no revisional jurisdiction. Only the High Court Division had revisional jurisdiction. Section 115 (2) has investigated the District Judge with revisional jurisdiction. In the circumstances the contention as of concurrent jurisdiction appears to be inconsistent. The District Judge's revisional jurisdiction under section 115(2) in our opinion, is restricted by his appellate jurisdiction as provided under section 21(1) of the Civil Courts Act. In other words, the District Judge can exercise revisional jurisdiction under section 115(2) only in respect of those cases where the value of the subject-matter does not exceed Taka 20,000. In all other cases, it is the High Court Division which exercises jurisdiction under section 115(1). Section 115(3) stands on a different footing and provides for a section revisional forum. Apart from section 115(3) the High Court Division, in our opinion, may under section 115(1) exercise its revisional jurisdiction in any case and its jurisdiction is not controlled by sub-section (2) of section 115. In the instant case the suit has been valued at Taka 1,00,000. For the reasons stated above, we are of the opinion that in the instant case the District Judge had no jurisdiction to entertain a revisional application under section 115(2) against the impugned order passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge. The instant revisional application before us is maintainable and competent.
